The test image shows a corn ear with pinkish-orange discoloration on kernels, some whitish mold, and infection concentrated toward the tip. This is a seed/ear disease.

Top candidates from the seed/pod classes: Fusarium_Disease, Gibberella_Disease, Aspergillus_Ear_Rot, Diplodia_Ear_Rot, Trichoderma_Ear_Rot. Let me view references one at a time.
Fusarium reference shows whitish mold on scattered kernels, mostly healthy ear. Test image has much more widespread pinkish-orange discoloration. Let me check Gibberella.
Gibberella shows dark reddish-brown mold concentrated at tip. Let me check Diplodia_Ear_Rot.
Aspergillus shows green powdery mold, not matching. Let me check Trichoderma.
Trichoderma shows dark blue-green/black mold on kernels. Not matching the pinkish-orange of the test image. Let me check Common_Smut and Head_Smut to cover more classes.
Common Smut shows large silvery-white galls with dark spore masses. Completely different from the test image. Let me check Diplodia_Ear_Rot pod reference.

Not matching either. Now let me revisit Fusarium with another reference, since the test image shows pinkish-orange discoloration on kernels which aligns with Fusarium's "whitish to pink" description. The test image's coloring leans more pink/orange than the first Fusarium reference I saw.

This Fusarium reference shows whitish-pink mold with some pinkish-orange discolored kernels, which is closer to the test image. The test image shows widespread pinkish-orange discoloration across many kernels with some whitish/grayish mold, and the ear appears dried/mature with husks pulled back.

Comparing all references:
- **Fusarium_Disease**: Whitish to pink mold on kernels, can be scattered or at tip. The pinkish-orange kernel discoloration in the test image matches well.
- **Gibberella_Disease**: Red/pink mold starting at tip. The Gibberella reference was darker, more reddish-brown.
- Others (Aspergillus, Trichoderma, Common_Smut, Diplodia) clearly don't match.

The test image shows pinkish-orange discolored kernels with some whitish mold, spread across the ear. This pattern, with the pink/salmon coloring on individual kernels, is most consistent with Fusarium ear rot (Fusarium_Disease).
